study.question: Can field-to-event message refinement help unified field/history evolution when event retrieval keys remain anchored to their initial visible representations? Which part of the reverse write accounts for its observed sign reversal?
study.hypothesis: Observation: g1-r0000-exchange_full improved macro AUC over g1-r0000-exchange_read_only by 0.0087959857892871, but all four original exchange arms lost to baseline-din. In the later family, g1-r0001-lowrank_feedback scored 0.8063642979653236 versus g1-r0001-lowrank_static 0.8111782509544756 (write effect -0.0048139529891520); the wide-value write effect was +0.0017698657468735. Thus a general benefit from reverse exchange is contradicted by the observed interaction with value design. Provisional mechanism: writing field information into the representation used for keys may perturb retrieval, while writing into values may provide useful conditional messages. Preserve initial event keys across depth and update only second-read values. The existing scores do not identify key drift or prove this hypothesis.

nearest_work.difference: Direct empirical parent and complete architectural inheritance. Replace the single scalar event_feedback with independent key_feedback and value_feedback switches; split the existing shared memory inputs without adding learned modules.

Pinned commit 90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d, lines 198-282 inspected: behavioral representation feeds both shared key and value projections. Our contrast preserves one initial key stream while field-conditioned messages alter only the value stream. We retain local shared query projections and field mixers; no per-field FFNs or content features are adopted.

Original primary https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10811v1 sections 5.1 and 5.3 inspected via web after registry detailed text was unavailable. LCA uses evolving behavioral representations for keys and values; our proposed intervention separately controls their response to a field-to-event write. This is not EST reproduction, a content-sparsity test, or a verified priority claim.

Pinned lines 187-266 inspected: query mixing and a sequence FFN precede key/value projections from the same updated sequence. Our local reverse write conditions history on evolving fields and separates its key/value destinations while retaining the inherited field self-attention mixer.

Original primary https://arxiv.org/html/2602.14110v2 sections 3.2-3.3 inspected via web. Inherit the general idea of repeated feature-conditioned retrieval only through the existing local model; do not implement its HeadMixing, per-head FFNs or request-sharing design. Independent control of reverse-write destinations is the local difference; novelty remains unverified.

Archived exact-version primary lines 271-283 and local baseline_reference.py inspected. DIN is an adapted single local-activation reference with unnormalized pooling; the candidate retains two rounds of softmax field/history exchange. Existing per-task and Logloss regressions prevent interpreting the incumbent macro AUC advantage as uniform superiority.

study.proposed_difference: Maintain E0 from authorized historical field/action embeddings plus valid-rank positions. First read uses E0 for both K and V. After first read/mix compute the inherited D=write(E0,F1) once. Set EK=mask(E0+0.5*k*D), EV=mask(E0+0.5*v*D). The second read uses K=key(LN(EK)) and V=value(LN(EV)) with shared existing projection/normalization parameters. Evolving task queries route the unchanged low-rank raw-event summary using EK. Candidate k=0,v=1 permits fields->history values->fields exchange while retaining initial key content. k,v in {0,1} form a complete factorial. Anchors are learned, differentiable E0 tensors, not frozen embeddings or detached gradients. No additional inputs, learned capacity or loss terms. Both endpoints are mathematical replacements of the prior static/full-feedback models; host numerical equivalence must be checked before treating their results as matched replications.
predictions: Primary directional prediction: value_feedback_only (01) beats feedback_neither (00) and feedback_both (11) in equal-weight validation macro AUC. A gain over both is required for preliminary support for useful value refinement protected by anchored keys; a gain over DIN alone is insufficient.

If key updates explain the low-rank write loss, 10-00 and 11-01 will be negative. Estimate value effects 01-00 and 11-10, key effects 10-00 and 11-01, and interaction 11-10-01+00. Report effect sizes rather than claiming significance from one seed.

Report all four task AUC/Logloss, macro Logloss, parameter counts, measured training and inference seconds, peak memory and latency. Selection remains macro AUC with frozen tie breakers, with no added per-task veto.

Exploratory slices use existing empty/1-16/17-64/>64 history bins, including positives/negatives from receipts. Check long-history click regression without selecting on that slice. Empty histories (6444 samples, only 13 buy positives) are a masking check and weak evidence about quality.

Expected registered parameters remain 32115012 (31793216 embedding, 321796 dense) at the supplied feature map, but host counts are authoritative. Additional shared LayerNorm execution and separate masked states may increase runtime slightly; there is no efficiency claim until measured.
falsifiers: 01 does not improve on 00: this implementation does not support beneficial field-conditioned value refinement. If 01 improves only on 11 but ties/loses to 00, removing key feedback explains recovery and coevolution has not earned its cost.

Key-only 10 improves on 00, or 11 improves on 01: the proposed key-path harm is contradicted for that conditional contrast. Mixed signs require an interaction explanation rather than a universal assertion.
Both one-path variants lose while 11 wins: complementary joint key/value adaptation is favored over the anchored-key hypothesis.

Endpoints fail shape, gradient, masking or replacement-equivalence checks, or a trial exceeds the fixed cap: classify implementation/resource failure separately from scientific counterevidence and do not infer mechanism effects from invalid arms.

No supported gain persists under later authorized paired seed repetitions, or measured cost exceeds the quality benefit: retain the static incumbent or DIN according to the declared quality/cost comparison, and report the mechanism as unsupported or preliminary.
alternative_explanations: Single seed and one pass cannot separate durable effects from initialization or optimization variation; matched forward work does not imply identical backward cost or active capacity.
Changing event keys affects both the second narrow read and final raw-value routing; this study identifies the combined key path, not the responsible layer.
With values enabled, field evolution changes later task queries even with anchored keys; anchored keys do not imply fixed attention weights.
No direct observations of attention collapse, semantic corruption or gradient instability are supplied; performance contrasts cannot establish those internal explanations.

The rank-32 reconstructed summary and its normalization may regularize or change optimization independently of information retention. The last factorial wide-versus-lowrank effects changed sign with feedback; it did not establish that preserving raw values helps.

Incumbent gains over DIN are concentrated in fav/buy rather than click/cart, and all task Logloss values worsened. Different calibration, task trade-offs and the benchmark auxiliary-label semantics could explain apparent aggregate gains.

Original earlier exchange and later low-rank-summary controls differ in readout/registered capacity, so their feedback-effect reversal cannot be interpreted as a single-factor comparison across families.
